candidates.title: @repo/schemas cannot be imported from a Playwright spec
candidates.evidence: packages/schemas package.json `exports` declares only an `import` condition; Playwright transpiles specs to CJS, so require() throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Specs currently import ../../packages/schemas/dist/index.js directly.
candidates.user_impact: None directly. But it blocks the `.parse() a real captured payload` pattern AGENTS.md calls the strongest sensor in this repo — which is exactly how BUG-20260822-public-posts-contract was caught. Fixing it makes every future e2e spec able to assert the contract.

candidates.title: AI Match % chip has no accessible role, label or test id
candidates.evidence: The score is a bare <span> with a text node (e.g. `62%`) plus a nested label span; journey 03 has to regex-scrape it out of the card's innerText.
candidates.user_impact: A screen-reader user cannot tell which number is the match score. Low severity but real; the score is the whole point of the search screen.

candidates.title: create_commit_summary_post tells agents `repo` is publishable, but the public projection drops metadata
candidates.evidence: MCP tool description says repo is 'served alongside the post on their public profile — so treat it as publishable'. publicPostResponseSchema omits metadata entirely, so it is never served. Docs and behaviour disagree in the SAFE direction.
candidates.user_impact: No leak today. But an agent author reading the description may put publishable-quality data in metadata expecting it to show, and a future change that starts serving metadata would leak repo names that were never disclosure-scanned (disclosure does not scan metadata).

candidates.title: visual-check scenario loading-state pattern is broken
candidates.evidence: scripts/visual/scenarios/public-profile.scenario.mjs fails at its loading step: mock(PROFILE_API, {delay: Infinity}) then goto(PROFILE) times out the navigation (net::ERR_ABORTED on the document) and unmock() is never reached.
candidates.user_impact: None — harness only. But it means the repo's own reference scenario cannot capture a loading state, so the four-state rule is unenforceable via that path.

candidates.title: dnd-kit keyboard sensor does not lift on the block grip button
candidates.evidence: The drag handle is keyboard-focusable but Space/Arrow/Space does not start a drag; a real pointer drag with intermediate moves works.
candidates.user_impact: Compounds BUG-20260822-layout-vertical-keyboard: the documented keyboard path into dnd-kit is also dead.

candidates.title: open-to-work switch has no accessible name
candidates.evidence: dashboard-profile-form.tsx renders a bare <button role="switch"> with no label; a screen reader announces 'switch, not pressed'.
candidates.user_impact: A screen-reader user cannot tell what the toggle controls — and it publicly advertises job-seeking status.

candidates.title: Malformed-email inline validation is unreachable behind native browser validation
candidates.evidence: The register form has no noValidate and the field is type=email, so `not-an-email` is caught by Chrome's native bubble and zod's 'Invalid email format' never renders.
candidates.user_impact: The user does get feedback, so this is low severity — but the app's own styled error is unreachable for the most common typo class and the native bubble ignores the app's dark mode.

candidates.title: Public profile payload includes each link's userId
candidates.evidence: GET /profile/:username returns links carrying userId to anonymous visitors.
candidates.user_impact: Minor internal-id exposure on a public endpoint; no direct harm, but it is gratuitous.

candidates.title: DELETE /me/layout/blocks/:id returns 400 when sent content-type: application/json with no body
candidates.evidence: 'Body cannot be empty…' — any standard API client that sets a default JSON content-type on DELETE hits this.
candidates.user_impact: None in the web app today; a rough edge for the MCP server and any external client.

candidates.title: Two journey tests are flaky under a full sequential run
candidates.evidence: In the 42-test full run, 03-recruiter-search.spec.ts:312 timed out after 60s waiting for getByRole('article') and 04-link-sharing.spec.ts:569 saw the pre-reorder link order. Re-running BOTH specs together immediately afterwards: 16/16 passed, relevance overlap 0 as expected. The search endpoint was independently probed at the same time and returned HTTP 200 with candidates, so quota exhaustion is ruled out.
candidates.user_impact: None directly — no product defect is demonstrated. It matters because REGRESSION compares against a baseline: two tests that fail ~sometimes make a clean night look like a regression, and a real regression look like noise. Diagnose before trusting any full-run comparison. Likely suspects: dev-server dep-optimisation reloads mid-run, and cross-journey load on one api process.

confirmed.title: Every public profile with a published post shows "Could not load posts. Please try again."
confirmed.user_impact: A developer publishes a post, shares their profile link — the single artifact this product exists to produce — and every visitor sees an error where the posts should be. Silent: an empty profile looks fine, so it only appears the moment someone actually publishes.
reproduction: Sign in as any user and publish at least one post (gabrielkochf already has 3 published).
Open http://localhost:5173/profile/gabrielkochf while signed out.
Wait ~12s for react-query to exhaust its 3 retries.
The Posts block renders 'Could not load posts. Please try again.'
confirmed.expected: The published posts render on the public profile.
confirmed.observed: Both Posts blocks show the error state. GET /profile/gabrielkochf/posts returns HTTP 200 with 3 valid rows — the failure is entirely client-side parsing.
confirmed.evidence: .visual/bug-public-posts.png ; live payload parsed through the shared schema fails with `invalid_type: expected record, received undefined at [0].metadata`
confirmed.suspected_cause: CONTRACT DRIFT. apps/api/src/infra/http/controllers/posts/posts-controller.ts:66 declares `publicPostResponseSchema = postResponseSchema.omit({ metadata: true })`, so the public feed never carries `metadata`. apps/web/src/lib/post-queries.ts:75 parses that response with `postSchema.array().parse(...)`, and packages/schemas/src/posts/index.ts:31 declares `metadata: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).nullable()` — nullable but NOT optional, therefore required. Every row fails.
confirmed.test_plan: Contract test first: `.parse()` a REAL captured payload from GET /profile/:username/posts through the schema the web client actually uses. Put it beside the schema in packages/schemas or in apps/api's posts controller tests. Then decide the fix at the CONTRACT level — either the public projection keeps `metadata` (nulled), or the web parses a public-specific schema. Do NOT simply widen postSchema.metadata to .optional(): AGENTS.md forbids widening a schema so a bad payload passes, and that would hide the drift rather than fix it. An e2e assertion in e2e/journeys/02-agent-posts.spec.ts already covers the user-visible half.
confirmed.found_by: journey-02 agent + verified independently against the running api and the rendered page

confirmed.title: An agent holding a PAT can publish its own post straight out of the review queue
confirmed.user_impact: The review queue tells the user 'Nothing here is public until you approve it', and the approve endpoint's own docs say it is 'the only way a machine-authored post becomes public'. Both are false: update_post{status:'published'} over a PAT releases a pending_review post itself. This is the consent gate for machine-written content about someone's real work.
reproduction: Mint a PAT through /dashboard/settings → Advanced settings → Create token.
Via the MCP server, create_post so it lands in pending_review.
Via the MCP server, update_post { id, status: 'published' }.
The post is public; the human never approved it.
confirmed.expected: A pending_review post can only be released by the human, through the review queue.
confirmed.observed: MCP returns 'Post updated ✅ … status: published' and the post is publicly visible.
confirmed.suspected_cause: apps/api/src/core/use-case/posts/shared/post-status-rules.ts — ALLOWED_STATUS_TRANSITIONS permits pending_review → published with no authType check, so a PAT-authenticated caller passes the same gate a session user does.
confirmed.test_plan: Unit test next to the use case in apps/api/src/core/**: a PAT-authenticated transition pending_review → published must be refused. Then an HTTP-level test via build-test-app.ts + server.inject. The e2e assertion already exists.
confirmed.found_by: journey-02 agent, driving the real apps/mcp server over stdio JSON-RPC

confirmed.title: Public profile links accept javascript:, data: and vbscript: URLs (latent stored XSS)
confirmed.user_impact: Any user can store a javascript:/data: URL as a public profile link. Today React 19 neutralises javascript: hrefs, so it is not exploitable through the current renderer — but React does NOT block data:, the defence is entirely the framework's, and the public profile is the page strangers visit. One renderer change, one dangerouslySetInnerHTML, or one non-React consumer of the API turns this into stored XSS against every visitor.
reproduction: Sign in and add a profile link with url `javascript:alert(1)`.
POST /links returns 201 and stores it verbatim.
GET /profile/:username serves it publicly.
apps/web/src/features/profile/components/profile-blocks.tsx:247 renders href={link.url} with no filtering.
confirmed.expected: Only http(s) URLs are accepted for anything that reaches an <a href> on a public page.
confirmed.observed: createLinkSchemaInput.safeParse accepts javascript:, JaVaScRiPt:, data:text/html, vbscript: and ftp:. Verified directly against the built schema.
confirmed.evidence: node -e with createLinkSchemaInput vs httpUrlSchema — links schema ACCEPTs all five, httpUrlSchema rejects all five
confirmed.suspected_cause: packages/schemas/src/links/index.ts uses a bare `z.string().url()` on linkSchema.url, createLinkSchemaInput.url and updateLinkSchemaInput.url. The repo ALREADY has the correct validator 30 lines away in packages/schemas/src/profile-blocks/index.ts — `httpUrlSchema` — whose own doc comment says: 'Every user-supplied URL that reaches an href or media src must use this.' The links module simply does not use it.
confirmed.test_plan: Contract test in packages/schemas: assert createLinkSchemaInput/updateLinkSchemaInput REJECT javascript:, data:, vbscript: and accept https:. That test fails today. Fix is `url: httpUrlSchema` in all three places. Then an api-level test via build-test-app.ts + server.inject asserting POST /links 400s on a javascript: URL. e2e/journeys/04-link-sharing.spec.ts already asserts no live non-http(s) href renders.
confirmed.found_by: journey-04 agent + verified independently against the built schema

confirmed.title: Every failed login or registration escapes as an unhandled promise rejection carrying the user's email
confirmed.user_impact: Wrong password is the single most common failure path in any app. Each one throws an uncaught rejection; Sentry's global unhandledrejection handler captures it in production. The registration variant's message body contains the user's email address ('User with email x@y already exists'), which sendDefaultPii:false does NOT scrub because it is in the message, not a PII field. So the app ships user emails to Sentry on a routine error path.
reproduction: Open / and submit the login form with a wrong password.
The visible error renders correctly and no tokens are written — but the console shows `uncaught: Invalid email or password`.
Repeat with the register form using an email that already exists: `uncaught: User with email '<email>' already exists`.
confirmed.expected: A rejected mutation is handled by the form; nothing reaches the global unhandledrejection handler.
confirmed.observed: Both forms produce uncaught rejections. Confirmed by e2e guard assertions in journey 01.
confirmed.suspected_cause: apps/web/src/features/auth/components/register-form.tsx:52 does handleSubmit(async (data) => { await onSubmit(data); reset(); }) and login-form.tsx:34 does handleSubmit(onSubmit), where onSubmit is auth-page.tsx's mutateAsync wrapper (lines 131/135). react-hook-form re-throws whatever the valid-handler rejects with, so every rejected mutateAsync escapes. Sentry init: apps/web/src/lib/report-error.ts:90.
confirmed.test_plan: Component test with @testing-library/react next to each form: submit, reject the mutation, assert the error renders AND that no unhandled rejection is produced. One fix covers both — catch in the submit handler, or use mutate instead of mutateAsync. The e2e guard assertions already cover the user-visible half.

confirmed.title: Blocks cannot be reordered vertically without a mouse — ArrowUp/ArrowDown are permanent no-ops
confirmed.user_impact: Reordering blocks is the primary thing a layout editor does, and vertically it is mouse-only. A keyboard or assistive-tech user cannot arrange their profile at all. Each futile press also fires a debounced PATCH that persists nothing.
reproduction: Open /dashboard/layout and focus the bottom block card.
Press ArrowUp ten times.
gridY never changes (observed 16 -> 16).
Sideways works: ArrowRight moves x 0->1, shift+ArrowLeft resizes w 12->11.
confirmed.expected: Arrow keys move a block vertically, the app's own documented keyboard substitute for drag.
confirmed.observed: ArrowUp/ArrowDown are no-ops; 10 presses produced 4 PATCH /me/layout/blocks/positions writes all carrying byte-identical geometry.
confirmed.suspected_cause: moveBlockBy in the layout feature's grid-utils.ts nudges by exactly +/-1 row then re-runs verticalCompactor.compact, which floats the block straight back. A single row can never clear a 4-6 row neighbour, and nothing accumulates because state is recompacted from the original gridY each press. The existing unit test at grid-utils.test.ts:236 passes only because it uses dy:-2 against an h:2 block — a full block height, which the card handler never sends.
confirmed.test_plan: Unit test beside grid-utils.test.ts using dy:-1 against a realistically tall neighbour — that test fails today and is the honest version of the existing one. Do NOT edit the existing test to make a fix pass; add the missing case. Then the e2e assertion in journey 05 covers the user-visible half.

confirmed.title: When /me/layout fails, the editor shows a fabricated default layout as if it were the user's own
confirmed.user_impact: On a 5xx the user sees a full grid of blocks they never created, an enabled toolbar, and the status line 'Changes save automatically'. Nothing says anything failed. A user who drags anything is editing a fabricated layout, and the autosave then persists it over their real one. This is the four-state rule AGENTS.md makes mandatory, and the failure mode is data loss rather than a blank screen.
reproduction: Open /dashboard/layout with GET /me/layout mocked to 500.
The page renders a complete default layout (e.g. a 'Profile header block' card) with a working toolbar.
No error copy appears anywhere.
confirmed.expected: An error state that tells the user the layout could not be loaded and does not offer editing.
confirmed.observed: buildDefaultLayout(viewport) is rendered as though it were saved data.
confirmed.suspected_cause: layoutQuery.isError is never read in apps/web/src/features/profile-layout/pages/profile-layout-page.tsx; on failure `full` is undefined and the code falls back to buildDefaultLayout(viewport).
confirmed.test_plan: Component test with @testing-library/react: render the page with the layout query in an error state, assert error copy is shown and the editor is not interactive. Fails today. RouteErrorState / the route-states helpers in apps/web/src/shared-components/route-states.tsx are the intended primitives.

confirmed.title: When /me fails, the dashboard profile panel is indistinguishable from a wiped account
confirmed.user_impact: On a 5xx the panel renders 'Your name', '@username', 'No description yet.' and a working Edit button. A user whose request merely failed is shown what looks like an account that lost all its data — and may re-enter everything over a transient error.
reproduction: Open /dashboard with GET /me mocked to 500.
The profile panel renders placeholder identity and an enabled Edit button.
No error copy appears.
confirmed.expected: An error state distinct from the empty state.
confirmed.observed: Empty-state copy is shown for a failed request.
confirmed.suspected_cause: meQuery.isError is never read in apps/web/src/features/dashboard/pages/dashboard-page.tsx. apps/web/src/lib/session.ts already documents this exact failure mode for expired sessions; a plain 5xx is still unhandled.
confirmed.test_plan: Component test with @testing-library/react asserting error copy renders when the /me query errors, and that it differs from the empty state. Fails today.
